haiku-low.q1: Only the SHA-256 hash is stored in api_tokens. Plaintext appears once, in the 201 response shown in the one-time dialog.
haiku-low.q2: They cannot get it back. Neither the server, support nor engineering can show it again. They create a new token.
haiku-low.q3: The server refuses it with a 4xx error telling the user to revoke a token first. No new token is created.
haiku-low.q4: On the very next request with the revoked token, which is rejected with 401, because validity is checked every request with no cache.
haiku-low.q5: All three get the same generic 401 body. The responses do not differ and do not reveal which case applied.
haiku-low.q6: The server computes SHA-256 of the presented token and selects the row by hash. The row must be not revoked and not expired.
haiku-low.q7: A successful API call triggers it when last-used is empty or more than 1 hour old. That check limits writes to about once per hour per token.
haiku-low.q9: Revoking sets the revoked time on the row. The token list then omits it, since the list shows only non-revoked, unexpired tokens.
haiku-low.q10: Another user's token id returns 404, the same as a nonexistent token. The document does not say what happens for an already revoked token.
haiku-low.q11: The row exists with its hash, but the user never sees the token and it cannot be recovered. The row counts toward the 10-token limit until revoked or expired. The user creates a new token and may revoke the lost one from the list.

sonnet.q1: It persists only the SHA-256 hash of the token (in the api_tokens row). The plaintext appears only in the 201 create response and the browser's one-time dialog while it is open; never stored, logged, or in analytics.
sonnet.q2: They can't. The token is shown exactly once and can't be shown again by server, support or engineering. They must create a new token.
sonnet.q3: The create is refused with a 4xx error whose message tells the user to revoke a token first. The transaction is rolled back and no row is inserted.
sonnet.q4: On the very next API request, because the server checks the database on every call with no caching of validity; it gets a 401.
sonnet.q5: The same 401 with a generic body for missing, unknown, revoked or expired tokens. The responses do not differ and do not reveal which case applied.
sonnet.q6: It computes the SHA-256 of the presented token and selects the row by that hash. The record is usable if a row exists and is not revoked and not expired; otherwise 401.
sonnet.q7: A valid API call where last-used is empty or more than 1 hour old triggers setting last-used to now. That condition limits it to about one write per token per hour.
sonnet.q9: Revoking sets the revoked time on the token's row (where id matches and the user is this user). The list only selects tokens that are not revoked and not expired, so the revoked token no longer appears.
sonnet.q10: Another user's token id returns 404, the same as a nonexistent token. For an already-revoked token, NOT STATED.
sonnet.q11: The row is saved in the database but the user never sees the token and can't get it back. The row still counts toward the 10-token limit until revoked or expired. The user creates a new token and may need to revoke the lost one from the list.
